h1: Bee Removal in NYC — Professional Nest Treatment and Removal
heroParagraph: Stinging insects in New York City — wasps, hornets, yellow jackets, carpenter bees, and ground-nesting bees — are more than a nuisance. An active nest inside a wall void, soffit, attic, or chimney is a structural problem that won't go away on its own. Wasp and hornet colonies can grow to thousands of individuals and build paper nests the size of basketballs inside wall cavities. If the nest is inside your structure, the entry points must be located, the nest treated and removed, and the openings sealed to prevent recolonization.
bodyParagraphs: Not all stinging insects are the same problem. Wasps, hornets, and yellow jackets build paper nests in wall voids, attics, eaves, and underground — they defend aggressively and can sting repeatedly. Carpenter bees drill perfectly round holes in wood eaves, decks, and fences to lay eggs — they don't sting aggressively but cause cumulative wood damage year after year. Ground-nesting bees burrow near landscaping and become defensive when their nest is disturbed. Honeybee colonies, when confirmed, are referred to a licensed beekeeper rather than treated. Each situation calls for a different approach, which is why we ask detailed questions before we quote.

Acting quickly matters. Stinging insect colonies are seasonal — nests are most aggressive in late summer when populations peak and foragers are protecting the nest. A small nest in April becomes a serious structural problem by August. If you've seen consistent insect activity around a specific entry point for more than a few days, the nest is already established.
signs: Consistent wasp or hornet traffic entering and exiting a single point on your structure — wall, soffit, chimney, fascia board, or ground opening
Buzzing sound inside walls or ceilings, particularly in the morning and evening
Paper nest visible under eaves, inside an attic vent, or attached to siding — gray or tan, papery texture
Round, perfectly drilled holes (about 3/8 inch diameter) in wood surfaces — carpenter bees
Increased stinging insect activity after rain, which drives foragers back toward the nest
Consistent traffic into a single wall or chimney opening with a waxy or sweet smell — usually honeybees, which we refer to a licensed beekeeper
treatmentApproach: Every job starts with identifying the species and locating the nest entrance. For wasp, hornet, and yellow jacket nests in wall voids, we treat the nest directly through the entry point, remove accessible nest material, and seal every opening to prevent recolonization. Carpenter bee treatments use residual dust applied directly into the nesting galleries, followed by wood sealant to close the holes. Ground-nesting bee and yellow jacket nests are treated at night when the colony is inactive. All treatments include entry point sealing. Honeybee colonies are referred to a licensed beekeeper after identification.

faqs.a: No, we do not treat honeybees. If an inspection confirms a colony is honeybees rather than wasps or hornets, we refer the situation to a licensed beekeeper instead of treating it ourselves.

faqs.q: Can I leave the nest alone if the insects aren't bothering me?
faqs.a: Not if the nest is inside your structure. A wasp or hornet nest inside a wall void will grow throughout the season and cause defensive stinging incidents as the colony expands. Even after the colony dies off in winter, the nest cavity can attract other pests and new colonies the following spring. Outdoor ground nests that aren't near foot traffic can sometimes be left alone until the colony dies naturally in fall — we'll tell you honestly if that's an option for your situation.

faqs.q: Why can't I just spray the nest myself?
faqs.a: Retail sprays don't penetrate wall voids where the nest is located, and spraying the entrance agitates the colony without eliminating it. Wasps and hornets become highly aggressive when the nest is threatened, and partial treatments often result in defensive stinging. Proper treatment requires locating the nest, treating it directly, and sealing entry points to prevent recolonization.

faqs.q: How long does nest removal take?
faqs.a: A straightforward exterior nest removal takes 1–2 hours. Wall void treatments that require locating hidden entry points or accessing attic spaces can take half a day. We give you a time estimate after the phone consultation so you can plan accordingly.

faqs.q: Do wasps and hornets come back after removal?
faqs.a: They can, if entry points aren't properly sealed. Wasps and hornets are attracted to old nest cavities, and scout insects from neighboring colonies can find and recolonize an unsealed void within the same season. Our service includes sealing all identified entry points. If you see activity return within 30 days, contact us — follow-up visits are handled as set in your service agreement.

faqs.q: How much does nest removal cost in NYC?
faqs.a: Pricing depends on the nest location, access, and severity — call (855) 930-5016 for a free phone quote and a clear price before any work begins.

faqs.q: What about carpenter bees — do they sting?
faqs.a: Female carpenter bees can sting but rarely do unless directly handled. Males, which are the ones hovering aggressively near your face, cannot sting at all. The real issue with carpenter bees is wood damage — they drill new galleries each year and the damage compounds over time. Woodpeckers also excavate carpenter bee galleries, causing additional damage.
